why: Range assignment (track / untrack a whole range) with range queries (is everything tracked?): a segment tree with lazy assignment over compressed endpoints, querying the minimum of a range.
hints: Each operation touches a whole range. What should a node remember so it does not update every point?
Collect every endpoint offline and compress; elementary segments [x_i, x_{i+1}) become leaves. A query is true iff the minimum over its segments is 1.

Lazy assignment: a fully covered node takes the value and remembers it; push the pending value to children before descending. O(log n) per operation. (A sorted list of disjoint intervals is the other classic solution.)
pitfalls: Half-open ranges: right maps to the segment just before it.
An assignment overrides any pending assignment below it; push before partial updates.
A query on never-touched points is false.
